rename.from: Nest sitemaps seem to 404 in Next.js 15
rename.to: Nested sitemaps seem to 404 in Next.js 15

body:
> Same problem but using Next.js 14.2.12

I have an app on 14.2.15 and it works just fine. It’s when I moved to 15 it stopped working for me.

If you guys use Yoast for the sitemap generation for the wordpress application, I suggest you to go through this ressource : https://robertmarshall.dev/blog/use-yoast-sitemap-with-next-js-and-headless-wordpress . I think the approach is not bad at all.

> If you guys use Yoast for the sitemap generation for the wordpress application, I suggest you to go through this ressource : https://robertmarshall.dev/blog/use-yoast-sitemap-with-next-js-and-headless-wordpress . I think the approach is not bad at all.

I don't use Wordpress, in the example I gave you can see it just doesn't work even with a static array returned.
I've also been having sitemap 404 issues on https://github.com/aelew/devterms using Next.js 15.0.3. Worked fine on 14. Google hasn't been able to read my dynamic sitemaps ever since I upgraded 🫤
@leerob I apologize for tagging you in this, but this feels like a major regression in Next 15 from Next 14, especially with multiple people experiencing it.
Also experiencing this. Working around it by creating a sitemap.xml folder with a route.tsx that exports a GET the "old fashioned way" for now.

Hi,

The docs is outdated current;y, since v15 the urls are the always prod ones, which is sitemap/0.xml. It’s more reasonable now which always have the .xml extension and identical between dev and prod.

We will update the docs shortly.

> Hi,
> 
> The docs is outdated current;y, since v15 the urls are the always prod ones, which is sitemap/0.xml. It’s more reasonable now which always have the .xml extension and identical between dev and prod.
> 
> We will update the docs shortly.

I don't think it's just a docs issue, even the prod URLs don't work. For example, https://www.coparesources.com/resources/sitemap/0.xml used to return properly in Next 14, however, now in Next 15 it's broken returning a 404.

@JamesSingleton we add a hash (e.g., `sitemap-<xyz>`)—so if you build your project, you should see where the exact path is (accessible in `next dev` or `next build`).

```
├   ├ /resources/sitemap-1jkbc8/0.xml
├   ├ /resources/sitemap-1jkbc8/1.xml
├   ├ /resources/sitemap-1jkbc8/2.xml
├   └ /resources/sitemap-1jkbc8/3.xml
```

@samcx is that new? Is that documented somewhere? I didn't see that anywhere which would be an undocumented breaking change. I also looked at the [v15 tag](https://github.com/vercel/next.js/releases/tag/v15.0.0) which I didn't see anything while searching `sitemap` that would indicate that this changed. 

Also, does that hash change on every single build?

> I didn't see that anywhere which would be an undocumented breaking change 👎🏼

Agreed, so that's on us! That's why we're updating the docs now.

> Also, does that hash change on every single build?

I think it's more like the CSS Modules where it doesn't change unless something else changes (in the process of figuring that out).

>I think it's more like the CSS Modules where it doesn't change unless something else changes (in the process of figuring that out).

Let me know what you find out because having dynamic sitemaps would mean things could change pretty frequently and therefore the hash would change. It's a little concerning we are roughly a month and a half out from the v15 release and this was just now _caught_ (probably not the right terminology). This is a major change in how users handle sitemaps, you're basically forcing everyone to now go into their Google Search Console, Bing, etc and update the sitemaps that search engines look at because of a change Next.js made and not one they deliberately made.
@JamesSingleton Thank you for the feedback! Will be sharing with the team.

issue.title: docs: update the outdated generate sitemaps doc with versioned changes
issue.body:
### What

The `generateSitempas`API page is outdated, we mentioned this change in the [v15 release blog](https://nextjs.org/blog/next-15) but not super highlighted with examples. 

> [Breaking] Remove .xml extension for dynamic sitemap routes and align sitemap URLs between development and production

Here we removed the legacy behavior from the description and added a new section of version history at the bottom for users to view and migrate

body:
Hi, Thanks for flagging the outdated description in the docs. The behavior is consistent between dev and prod now since v15 RC release, you should now visit `resources/sitemap/0.xml`rather than `resources/sitemap.xml/0`.

We mentioned it as a breaking change in the [v15 blog](https://nextjs.org/blog/next-15)) but might it didn't highlight well with examples.
> [Breaking] Remove .xml extension for dynamic sitemap routes and align sitemap URLs between development and production ([PR](https://github.com/vercel/next.js/pull/65507))

I filed a PR (https://github.com/vercel/next.js/pull/73547) to updated the docs

@huozhi  that doesn’t close this issue out. I get that now between local development and production the URLs are the same, that’s create.

My issue is that Next now adds a hash to the URL as @samcx  pointed out. That’s a BREAKING CHANGE compared to the behavior that was there in Next 14. Going from `/resources/sitemap/0.xml` in production with Next 15 to now having `/resources/sitemap-1jkbc8/0.xml` is breaking. Furthermore, not knowing what causes the hash to change is concerning. Users now have to go into wherever they have their sitemaps and update it. If that hash changes whenever a new item is added, that’s going to cause A LOT is headaches for users.
